checks.note: The diff confirms syncPaymentMethod retries the invoice with no local lock/write (so GraceTarget.matches and the FOR UPDATE re-read cannot block it), but the finding's required verification — that cancelAtStripeForGrace/cancelSubscriptionImmediately null stripeSubscriptionId without voiding the open invoice at Stripe, and that the invoice.paid handler acks on a findByStripeSubscriptionId miss — depends on method bodies, the webhook handler, and SubscriptionLifecycleIT, none of which are in the shown hunks.

updateSubscriptionDefaultPaymentMethod builds its idempotency key as "sub-pm-" + subscriptionId + paymentMethodId with no per-attempt component, so re-setting a previously used card within Stripe's 24h window sends an identical request and Stripe replays the cached response without executing the update, leaving the old default in place. Stripe's documented semantics (24h key retention, replay of original response for identical requests) match the finding's caveat.

payLatestOpenInvoice does pay only sub.getLatestInvoice() with no loop over other open invoices, but the claimed consequence depends on the invoice.paid handler and RECOVERABLE_ON_PAYMENT set, which are not in these hunks; whether ACTIVE is restored and pastDueSince cleared without re-checking the subscription's Stripe status cannot be verified here.

The hunk shows save(existing) then syncPaymentMethodToSubscriptions(parentId, request.paymentMethodId()) with no visible lock, but the finding's verification requires confirming no per-user serialization exists anywhere: the top of savePaymentMethod, the StripeCustomer entity (possible @Version), and SubscriptionService.syncPaymentMethodToSubscriptions are not in the diff, so a lock or claim there cannot be ruled out.

matches.note: R2 identifies the same defect (saving a card never resumes a PAUSED subscription, no Stripe resume call exists) with the same consequence of the grace sweep cancelling it.
R6 captures the swallowed-exception/silent-204 fragment of F2 but misses the architectural core: synchronous Stripe calls inside the save-card request with no durable retry/outbox.
No reported finding addresses the lack of distinction between retryable and permanent Stripe failures in the catch handling.
